title: The Dot Product and the Angle Between Vectors
trouble: Students treat the dot product as a vector rather than a number.

blocks.html: Adding vectors gives a vector. A different product of two vectors gives a single number that measures how much they point the same way. It is the key to angles between vectors.

$$\langle a, b \rangle \cdot \langle c, d \rangle = ac + bd \qquad\text{and}\qquad \mathbf{u} \cdot \mathbf{v} = |\mathbf{u}||\mathbf{v}|\cos\theta,$$ where $\theta$ is the angle between them. So $\cos\theta = \dfrac{\mathbf{u} \cdot \mathbf{v}}{|\mathbf{u}||\mathbf{v}|}$, and $\mathbf{u}$ and $\mathbf{v}$ are perpendicular exactly when $\mathbf{u} \cdot \mathbf{v} = 0$.

Put $\mathbf{u}$ and $\mathbf{v}$ tail to tail; the third side of the triangle is $\mathbf{u} - \mathbf{v}$. The law of cosines says $$|\mathbf{u} - \mathbf{v}|^2 = |\mathbf{u}|^2 + |\mathbf{v}|^2 - 2|\mathbf{u}||\mathbf{v}|\cos\theta.$$ In components the left side is $$(a - c)^2 + (b - d)^2 = |\mathbf{u}|^2 + |\mathbf{v}|^2 - 2(ac + bd).$$ Comparing the two gives $ac + bd = |\mathbf{u}||\mathbf{v}|\cos\theta$.

blocks.name: vectors2d
blocks.cap: Drag the tips. The dot product is positive for an acute angle, zero for a right angle and negative for an obtuse angle.

blocks.title: Perpendicular
blocks.q: Find $k$ so that $\langle k, 3 \rangle$ is perpendicular to $\langle 2, -4 \rangle$.

blocks.html: Treating the dot product as a vector, for example writing $\langle 3, -2 \rangle \cdot \langle 4, 5 \rangle = \langle 12, -10 \rangle$. Multiply matching components and then add; the result is one number. Its sign alone tells you whether the angle is acute ($+$), right ($0$) or obtuse ($-$).
